film: Minase launch film, 41 s, 16:9: dense white UI collages alternating with sparse lines, a quiet black reveal, dark stock footage with typed lines, three logo appearances

shots.see: white; UI collage cards (white, blue accent) assemble and drift
near-black footage; cards gone; one silhouette, type words fly in
white; a soft blue orb sits behind italic word-swaps
shots.words: Not because the product is weak.

shots.see: white; collage cards return around the line; a product page and prompt box scale in
shots.words: product is weak / Because nobody ever showed it the way you see it.

shots.see: white; a single bullet dot leads the typed line
shots.words: A product gets a few seconds to make sense. That's it.

shots.see: dark stock footage; an up-arrow chip is dropped into the line, then carried into the next scene
shots.words: And in those seconds, people don't read. They feel.

shots.see: black; the chip becomes the blue hexagon mark, which sits left of the name
shots.words: So that's what Minase builds. The moment it clicks.

shots.see: white; arrow chip pushes the type; cards and a dashboard flow past; a circular diagram resolves
shots.words: From a launch nobody noticed to a launch that moves. Same product, different world.

shots.see: dark stock footage; words stack and swap in place over typing hands
shots.words: Every frame, every second, every decision.

shots.see: white; a scrolling word list with an arrow carries to the final word
shots.words: With Minase, it's covered, crafted and ready to launch.

shots.see: dark stock footage; a typed prompt line with the chip, over a person at a table
shots.words: What if today was the day people finally saw it?

shots.see: white to grey fade; the hexagon mark and name resolve and hold

carrier.what: UI collage cards plus a small up-arrow chip that is dropped into a line and becomes the brand mark

signature_moment.what: the first music hit flips white UI collage to a silhouette at a desk and the words 'Nobody's watching it' fly in: the viewer's problem, felt, in one frame

hook.what: 'You built something good. Nobody's watching it.' over a dense collage that flips to a silhouette: the viewer's problem, no brand

turn.what: 'That's it' on an empty white ground, then 'And in those seconds, people don't read. They feel.'

proof.what: dense UI plates and a diagram, then one line of what the brand does

close.what: 'What if today was the day people finally saw it?' then the end card

image_use.how_moved: simplified cards, dashboards and prompt boxes fly in, tilt and recede as a collage; a prompt box types its line
word-by-word builds, in-place word swaps in one slot, giant words behind cards
dark stock footage of people at desks under typed lines, cut on a music hit

atlas_style_world.why: no atlas world is neutral kinetic type on white and black with UI cards; the nearest is an editorial/minimal type world
atlas_style_world.gap: the atlas lacks a default 'carrier-led kinetic type on neutral ground' world; this grammar is the launch default, see references/launch-grammar.md

sound.structure: voice-over from 0 s (a sentence per beat, lines match the on-screen type); music bed in from 0.3 s; hits at 0.35, 1.1, 5.8, 9.9, 12.5, 19.0, 27.0, 31.7; a thin break at 38-39 s before the end card
sound.mix_notes: bed about -15 LUFS under the voice with no hard duck; clicks only on word swaps (about 5 per 10 s); end card holds on the bed's tail

what_to_take: The copy is the spine: one thought per beat, second person, built word by word, with one emphasised word per line.
The brand appears small, 3 times at most (mid reveal, one pop, end card): the film's look carries the brand.
Alternate dense UI collages with a single small line on an empty ground; the ground flips on a music hit.
Hand an element from beat to beat: a chip dropped into a line becomes the mark.
Mixed media is fine when type leads: dark stock footage under typed lines is the breathing space.
what_not_to_copy: its copy, its name or its hexagon mark
its exact collage cards and stock footage
its blue palette and serif/mono type pairing
corrections: refs.mjs counted 13 cuts at the 0.4 threshold (3.1 per 10 s) and 21 shots: these are ground flips (white to dark footage and back, dense to sparse) and fast in-frame changes that fall on music hits. Type, chips and cards carry across most of them. Read the film as 12 beats, not 21 shots.

the sound-mode guess 'vo' is right: this film has a voice-over that reads each on-screen line (92 words). The owner's target note says on-screen type carries the narration; for Minase the type and the voice say the same thing, one thought per beat.
the scene-score shot list misses morphs, word swaps and masks: the beat table in beats.json is the real structure.
